children: *USDA Lifts Outlook for Soybean Output in WASDE, Versus Analyst Expectations for Cuts
*USDA Reduces Outlook for Corn Production Less Than Expected by Analysts
*Forecast for U.S. Corn, Soybean Stockpiles Slide for 2026/27 Marketing Year, Says USDA
USDA Cuts Corn Output Projections, Lifts Soybean Forecast
U.S. farmers are expected to harvest less corn than anticipated and produce more soybeans this fall, according to the Department of Agriculture.

The USDA said corn planted this spring and grown over the summer will produce less bushels than previously forecast - falling after last year's record-sized yields - in its monthly WASDE report published Friday.

The USDA said corn being harvested this fall is expected to produce 15.8 billion bushels, with a yield of 178.5 bushels an acre. Both figures are lower than projected by the agency in August, which pegged corn production at 16.01 billion bushels with a yield of 180.7 bushels an acre.

Soybean production is projected at 4.54 billion bushels for this fall, with a yield of 52.8 bushels an acre. Last month, the USDA projected production at 4.52 billion bushels, with a yield of 52.7 bushels an acre.

The USDA's corn projections landed above what analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal expected, while analysts projected soybean production and yields to drop from the prior month. Surveyed analysts forecast corn production at 15.77 billion bushels, with a yield of 178.1 bushels an acre. Soybean production was seen at 4.49 billion bushels, with a yield of 52.5 bushels an acre.

Grain futures trading on the CBOT were mixed following the report. Most-active corn futures rose 1%, after trading down 0.8% before the report. Soybeans fell 1.8%, slightly more than before the report was published. Futures for wheat, which did not get any updates to its output figures, fell 2.3%.

Trader reaction to the data is seen as restrained by some analysts. "The market clearly [is] meeting these numbers with some skepticism," Doug Bergman, director of agricultural trading with RCM Alternatives, said in a note published following the WASDE's release.
